mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% over the past three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes a decline in corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction permits (HOUST) and consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates a contraction in household demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 5% in the last 3 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline > 5% in the last 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90% of its 2007 peak signals an imminent recession, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 90, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) signals a weakening economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 is declining, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 4.0% annually signals accelerating inflation, which typically triggers a monetary policy response that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 4.0%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals worsening labor market conditions, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5% and PAYEMS declines, or the Rank IC is negative over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95% of its 2007 peak signals an immediate supply shock, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
